title: Fire Safety on Site
whatItIs: A fire needs heat, fuel and oxygen: if one is missing, it can't start. On site that means controlling hot work, flammable materials, waste and smoking, and knowing the right extinguisher.

keyFacts.text: Steps MUST be taken to prevent the risk of injury from fire or explosion, so far as reasonably practicable.
You MUST NOT do work with a particular fire risk unless you've been suitably instructed.
Fire-fighting equipment MUST be easy to get to, signed, examined and tested at suitable intervals, and maintained.

keyFacts: Keep a fire watch during hot work and for at least an hour after, then check again at 2 hours.
Extinguishers are for small fires or to aid escape. Don't delay calling the fire and rescue service.
No smoking on site except in designated smoking areas, away from buildings and flammables.

visual.caption: Which extinguisher? A coloured zone on the red body shows the contents

items.title: Water
items.text: Wood, paper, textiles, solids. NOT on liquid, electrical or metal fires.

items.title: Foam
items.text: Liquid fires; also wood and paper. NOT on electrical or metal fires.

items.title: Dry powder (blue zone)
items.text: Liquid and electrical fires (multi-purpose: solids too). NOT on metal.

items.title: Carbon dioxide (CO2)
items.text: Liquid and electrical fires. NOT on metal fires.

a.label: Water extinguisher
points: For wood, paper, cloth and solids
Never on electrical or liquid fires

onTheTest.question: A fire starts in an electrical distribution board. Which extinguisher should you use?
onTheTest.why: HSG168: for electrical items use a carbon dioxide (CO2) or dry powder extinguisher. Water and foam must not be used on electrical fires.

onTheTest.question: You've finished welding for the day. What fire watch does HSE guidance advise?
options: An hour's watch, then a check at 2 hours
None once the torch is off
A quick look before you go
onTheTest.why: HSG168: keep a continuous fire watch for at least an hour after hot work ends, then at least one more check two hours after it ends.

traps: Never use water on electrical or burning liquid fires.
Don't tackle a large fire: putting out larger fires is the fire and rescue service's job.
Keep fire doors closed: never wedge them open.
Keep the fire watch during breaks in hot work too, not just at the end.

sources.doc: HSE HSG168 Fire safety in construction
